note: Re-judged 2026-10-18 (independent auditor, after 2e4be94ae3). Read at rfc/full/rfc7950.txt Section 9.5.1: "The lexical representation of a boolean value is a string with a value of "true" or "false". These values MUST be in lowercase." The units changed only from validateYangType to ValidateType, the same producer path. validateBoolean accepts exactly "true" and "false"; the negative requires ErrTypeType 'expected boolean' for True, FALSE, TRUE, yes and 1, so a case-folding comparison would turn it red. Ze's config spelling enable/disable is rewritten by NormalizeBool (case-sensitive) before the validator, and TestBooleanConfigSpellingRefused pins that the validator itself refuses them.
